subject: Temporary latency waiver & remediation credit plan — NimbleHealth pilot
messages:
From: Samantha Coleman <samantha@nimblehealth.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: NimbleHealth SRE Team <sre@nimblehealth.ai>
Date: 2025-10-29T08:22:00Z
Subject: Request: temporary SLA latency waiver + monthly remediation credits

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking a look at our pilot plan this week. Quick summary of where we ended up in the SRE review: our production inference workload for the next 3 months will have predictable burst windows (weekday 09:00–11:30 PDT) driven by real-time triage. During those windows our p95 can spike to ~280–320ms for single-request paths.

Given that, we need to ask Redwood for a temporary latency waiver (p95 latency target relaxed from 200ms to 300ms) for a defined pilot period, and an accompanying remediation credit schedule in the event of service degradation outside of that bounded exception. Procurement has asked for a concrete monthly credit calculation so they can sign off.

Attached is the SRE questionnaire excerpt and the production traces that motivated the ask (NimbleHealth_SRE_requirements.pdf).

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Offer a 90-day waiver starting Nov 1, 2025 with p95=300ms for the specified windows only
- Provide a tiered monthly credit schedule tied to monthly uptime and p95 exceedance (we prefer a 3-tier approach rather than a flat cap)

If possible, we'd like a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a technical sync to finalize routing fallbacks and cache TTLs before Nov 1.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a quick call.

Best,
Samantha Coleman
Head of Platform, NimbleHealth
---
Attachment: NimbleHealth_SRE_requirements.pdf (pdf, 1 page)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Coleman <samantha@nimblehealth.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-29T13:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA latency waiver + monthly remediation credits

Hi Samantha — thanks for the detail and the traces. We can absolutely work with a time‑boxed exception, but a few practical points and a proposal below.

Quick notes:
- We prefer to limit any formal SLA waiver to clearly scoped windows and a fixed pilot timeframe (your Nov 1 start works).
- For credits, Redwood typically uses a monthly tiered formula that scales with the magnitude and duration of the SLO miss. We can map to your three tiers.

Proposed pilot terms (outline):
1) Waiver scope: 2025-11-01 to 2026-01-30 (90 days)
   - Waiver applies only during weekday 09:00–11:30 PDT for the specified NimbleHealth production project
   - p95 latency allowance during waiver windows: 300ms (baseline p95 target remains 200ms outside windows)
2) Credit schedule (monthly, tiered):
   - Tier A (minor): p95 exceeds 300ms for >2% of requests in the month => 5% of that month's invoice credited
   - Tier B (moderate): p95 exceeds 300ms for 2–10% of requests => 15% credit
   - Tier C (severe): p95 exceeds 300ms for >10% of requests OR sustained unavailability (>30 minutes total) => 40% credit
   - Upper cap: credits cannot exceed 50% of monthly invoice (we can negotiate escrow treatment if you need fixed cap exceptions)
3) Remediation & MAP
   - Joint tech sync prior to Nov 1 to confirm routing fallback and prefix cache configuration
   - Weekly health check during pilot, and a retrospective at pilot end

Questions for you (to finalize):
- Do you want credits paid as invoice offset or into a credit escrow pool?
- Can you confirm the exact project id and any subdomains so we can scope routing rules?

Next steps: if this outline is reasonable I will loop Legal for a short addendum and share an RNWD redline. Laura / Marissa — can you advise on the quickest route for a 90-day exception addendum?

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0129

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Samantha Coleman <samantha@nimblehealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-10-29T15:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA latency waiver + monthly remediation credits

Samantha / Rishi — looping Legal in. High level: we can do a 90‑day exception as an addendum, but procurement needs clear language on credit remediation, reporting cadence, and an explicit termination trigger for the waiver. I attached an initial redline with proposed language (RNWD-SLA-provisional-redline.docx).

Key legal points we will include in the addendum:
- Waiver is strictly time‑boxed and scoped to the listed hostnames/project IDs
- Credits are computed based on our server-side telemetry; NimbleHealth may request audit logs within 14 days of a credit claim
- Cap: we propose the 50% monthly cap that Rishi suggested; if you require escrow we can include that but it will affect billing/payment terms
- Emergency rollback: Redwood will use automated fallback routing if degradation exceeds Tier C thresholds for >30 consecutive minutes; that fallback is exempt from waiver and will not count toward credits

Samantha — please confirm whether NimbleHealth requires credits to be issued as direct invoice offsets or prefers a third-party escrow holding. We can prepare the DocuSign envelope once that's confirmed.

Laura Bennett
VP, Legal — Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.ai

Laura / Rishi — thanks, that looks fine from our side. NimbleHealth prefers invoice offsets (simpler for our finance ops). We accept the 50% monthly cap for the pilot and will request telemetry access for audit within the 14-day window if needed.

We accept the proposed MAP: technical sync Thursday 2025-10-30 16:00 PDT, weekly health checks, pilot retrospective on 2026-01-31. I've requested calendar invites.

Short confirm: we agree to the waiver scope and the tiered credit structure as outlined. Please send the addendum for signature and the DocuSign link.

Samantha
